title: Early Return to Competition After vNOTES Ovarian Cystectomy in a Professional Athlete: A Case Report

segments.heading: Abstract
segments.text: There are currently no studies that have evaluated return-to-sport or return-to-competition outcomes in professional athletes following gynecologic surgery. In addition, reports describing return to competition after vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) in professional athletes are extremely limited. The present report focuses on early return to competition following vNOTES ovarian cystectomy in a professional athlete.

segments.heading: Abstract
segments.text: We report the case of a 20-year-old nulliparous professional bowler who underwent vNOTES ovarian cystectomy for a 9-cm left serous cystadenoma. The operation time was 66 minutes with minimal blood loss, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day three. She resumed training on postoperative day four, became asymptomatic by day 10, and returned to a national competition on postoperative day 23, finishing fourth.

segments.heading: Abstract
segments.text: This case demonstrates an exceptionally rapid postoperative recovery and represents one of the earliest documented returns to competition following gynecologic adnexal surgery, suggesting that vNOTES may offer distinct advantages for athletes who require preservation of abdominal wall integrity and rapid restoration of core function.

segments.heading: Introduction
segments.text: Minimally invasive surgery is the standard treatment for benign ovarian tumors. In conventional laparoscopy, transabdominal port placement is required, which can result in postoperative pain, muscle injury, and delayed recovery. For professional athletes, whose performance depends heavily on abdominal and core muscle function, abdominal wall trauma may significantly delay return to sport.

segments.heading: Introduction
segments.text: Vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) is a minimally invasive surgical approach that enables access to the peritoneal cavity through the vagina, thereby avoiding abdominal wall incisions. This technique is increasingly recognized in gynecology for its potential to reduce postoperative pain and facilitate faster functional recovery. vNOTES has been reported in randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews to provide superior outcomes compared with laparoscopy, including reduced postoperative pain, shorter hospital stays, and faster return to daily activities [-].

This technique is increasingly recognized in gynecology for its potential to reduce postoperative pain and facilitate faster functional recovery. vNOTES has been reported in randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews to provide superior outcomes compared with laparoscopy, including reduced postoperative pain, shorter hospital stays, and faster return to daily activities [ [BIBR:REF1 1] - [BIBR:REF4 4] ].

segments.heading: Introduction
segments.text: However, how these advantages translate to athletic populations remains largely unexamined. In gynecologic surgery, no studies have evaluated return-to-sport or return-to-competition outcomes. Because vNOTES causes no abdominal wall trauma, it may offer greater benefits than laparoscopy for athletes, whose performance depends on core stability. Nevertheless, empirical data to support this concept are lacking.

segments.heading: Introduction
segments.text: Here, we present a case of a professional athlete who underwent vNOTES ovarian cystectomy and achieved an exceptionally rapid return to competition, providing the first sport-specific recovery insight in the context of gynecologic minimally invasive surgery.

segments.heading: Case presentation
segments.text: A 20-year-old nulliparous professional bowler presented with lower abdominal pain. She competed at the national level, and her sport required repetitive trunk rotation and core muscle engagement. She had no notable past medical, surgical, or family history. Physical examination revealed a soft, non-tender abdomen, and bimanual pelvic examination identified a mobile, enlarged mass in the lower abdomen, estimated to be around the size of a large hen’s egg.

segments.heading: Case presentation
segments.text: Transvaginal ultrasonography revealed a unilocular cystic lesion in the left adnexal region measuring 72 × 58 mm, with benign features. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed a unilocular cyst arising from the left ovary measuring 92 × 72 × 60 mm, showing low signal intensity on T1-weighted MRI and high intensity on T2-weighted MRI (Figure 1).

segments.heading: Case presentation
segments.text: The preoperative diagnosis was serous cystadenoma of the left ovary. Surgery was indicated based on the size of the cyst. Considering that the patient was scheduled to participate in a national bowling tournament within one month, vNOTES ovarian cystectomy was chosen to avoid abdominal incisions and preserve athletic performance. The procedure was performed under general anesthesia. The peritoneal cavity was accessed transvaginally (Figure 2).
segments.text_with_reference_markers: The preoperative diagnosis was serous cystadenoma of the left ovary. Surgery was indicated based on the size of the cyst. Considering that the patient was scheduled to participate in a national bowling tournament within one month, vNOTES ovarian cystectomy was chosen to avoid abdominal incisions and preserve athletic performance. The procedure was performed under general anesthesia. The peritoneal cavity was accessed transvaginally (Figure [FIG:FIG2 2] ).

segments.heading: Case presentation
segments.text: The left ovary was enlarged to the size of a large hen’s egg, and the cyst was carefully exteriorized through the vagina. The cyst wall was punctured extracorporeally, and its contents were aspirated; extracorporeal cystectomy with ovarian reconstruction was completed without complications. The operation time was 66 minutes with minimal blood loss. The specimen was a thin-walled cyst (Figure 3), and histopathology confirmed a benign serous cystadenoma.

The operation time was 66 minutes with minimal blood loss. The specimen was a thin-walled cyst (Figure [FIG:FIG3 3] ), and histopathology confirmed a benign serous cystadenoma.

segments.heading: Case presentation
segments.text: Postoperatively, the patient reported minimal pain, was ambulating independently on postoperative day one, and was discharged on postoperative day three. She resumed training on postoperative day four with only mild discomfort, with no limitation in performance. By postoperative day 10, she was completely asymptomatic, and by day 23, she competed in a national tournament, placing 4th.

segments.heading: Discussion
segments.text: Multiple randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews have demonstrated that vNOTES offers several advantages over conventional laparoscopy, including reduced postoperative pain, shorter hospitalization, and decreased analgesic requirements [-]. A series of 1,000 cases also showed low complication rates and high reproducibility [].
segments.text_with_reference_markers: Multiple randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews have demonstrated that vNOTES offers several advantages over conventional laparoscopy, including reduced postoperative pain, shorter hospitalization, and decreased analgesic requirements [ [BIBR:REF1 1] - [BIBR:REF4 4] ]. A series of 1,000 cases also showed low complication rates and high reproducibility [ [BIBR:REF5 5] ].

segments.heading: Discussion
segments.text: However, in the field of gynecology, no studies have evaluated postoperative return-to-sport (RTP) or return-to-competition outcomes. Existing literature addresses only return to daily activity, and no data describe the recovery of sport-specific function in athletes.

segments.heading: Discussion
segments.text: In contrast, the sports medicine literature includes data on postoperative return to competition after minimally invasive surgery. In a large series of athletes undergoing laparoscopic repair for inguinal disruption, Piozzi et al. reported that 94.4% of athletes returned to full sports activity within approximately four weeks []. Their findings indicate that preservation of the abdominal wall and minimizing postoperative pain are critical determinants of athletic recovery.
segments.text_with_reference_markers: In contrast, the sports medicine literature includes data on postoperative return to competition after minimally invasive surgery. In a large series of athletes undergoing laparoscopic repair for inguinal disruption, Piozzi et al. reported that 94.4% of athletes returned to full sports activity within approximately four weeks [ [BIBR:REF6 6] ]. Their findings indicate that preservation of the abdominal wall and minimizing postoperative pain are critical determinants of athletic recovery.

segments.heading: Discussion
segments.text: In the present case, the patient resumed training on postoperative day 4 and returned to competition on day 23. This recovery rate is comparable to, or even faster than, that reported in sports-related laparoscopic procedures. Because vNOTES completely avoids abdominal wall incisions, it may offer superior recovery potential for athletes whose performance relies on core muscle function.

segments.heading: Discussion
segments.text: Although this is a single case and its generalizability is limited, it provides the first academic insight into return-to-sport outcomes following gynecologic surgery and highlights an important but previously unexplored clinical dimension. Long-term follow-up data were not available in the present case. In addition, postoperative scarring or adhesion formation could not be assessed, as no second-look surgery or imaging specifically evaluating adhesions was performed.

segments.heading: Conclusions
segments.text: vNOTES ovarian cystectomy enabled extremely rapid functional recovery and early return to competition in a professional athlete. In this case, the patient resumed training on postoperative day 4 and returned to national-level competition on postoperative day 23, representing an exceptionally early recovery trajectory following gynecologic adnexal surgery.

segments.heading: Conclusions
segments.text: In the absence of evidence evaluating return-to-sport or return-to-competition outcomes after gynecologic surgery, this case highlights the potential clinical value of vNOTES for athletes who require preservation of abdominal wall integrity and rapid restoration of core function. Further studies with larger cohorts are warranted to systematically assess sport-specific recovery outcomes following gynecologic surgery, as the present findings are based on a single case.

[b00022] Case presentation
The preoperative diagnosis was serous cystadenoma of the left ovary. Surgery was indicated based on the size of the cyst. Considering that the patient was scheduled to participate in a national bowling tournament within one month, vNOTES ovarian cystectomy was chosen to avoid abdominal incisions and preserve athletic performance. The procedure was performed under general anesthesia. The peritoneal cavity was accessed transvaginally (Figure 2).

[b00023] Case presentation
The left ovary was enlarged to the size of a large hen’s egg, and the cyst was carefully exteriorized through the vagina. [b00025] Discussion
Multiple randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews have demonstrated that vNOTES offers several advantages over conventional laparoscopy, including reduced postoperative pain, shorter hospitalization, and decreased analgesic requirements [-]. A series of 1,000 cases also showed low complication rates and high reproducibility [].

[b00026] Discussion
However, in the field of gynecology, no studies have evaluated postoperative return-to-sport (RTP) or return-to-competition outcomes. Existing literature addresses only return to daily activity, and no data describe the recovery of sport-specific function in athletes.

[b00027] Discussion
In contrast, the sports medicine literature includes data on postoperative return to competition after minimally invasive surgery. In a large series of athletes undergoing laparoscopic repair for inguinal disruption, Piozzi et al. reported that 94.4% of athletes returned to full sports activity within approximately four weeks []. Their findings indicate that preservation of the abdominal wall and minimizing postoperative pain are critical determinants of athletic recovery.

[b00028] Discussion
In the present case, the patient resumed training on postoperative day 4 and returned to competition on day 23. This recovery rate is comparable to, or even faster than, that reported in sports-related laparoscopic procedures. Because vNOTES completely avoids abdominal wall incisions, it may offer superior recovery potential for athletes whose performance relies on core muscle function.

[b00029] Discussion
Although this is a single case and its generalizability is limited, it provides the first academic insight into return-to-sport outcomes following gynecologic surgery and highlights an important but previously unexplored clinical dimension. Long-term follow-up data were not available in the present case. In addition, postoperative scarring or adhesion formation could not be assessed, as no second-look surgery or imaging specifically evaluating adhesions was performed.

[b00030] Conclusions
vNOTES ovarian cystectomy enabled extremely rapid functional recovery and early return to competition in a professional athlete. In this case, the patient resumed training on postoperative day 4 and returned to national-level competition on postoperative day 23, representing an exceptionally early recovery trajectory following gynecologic adnexal surgery.

[b00031] Conclusions
In the absence of evidence evaluating return-to-sport or return-to-competition outcomes after gynecologic surgery, this case highlights the potential clinical value of vNOTES for athletes who require preservation of abdominal wall integrity and rapid restoration of core function. Further studies with larger cohorts are warranted to systematically assess sport-specific recovery outcomes following gynecologic surgery, as the present findings are based on a single case.
